title: measure_packet_motion.py: --xmax with missing or non-numeric value crashes with an unhandled traceback
detail: No guard for --xmax as the final argv entry or followed by non-numeric text; reproduced: `measure_packet_motion.py a b --xmax` raises IndexError instead of exiting 2 with usage.
recommended_fix: Validate the flag arity/value before indexing (e.g. argparse or an explicit index+parse check) and exit 2 with a usage message.

title: motion-strip: user-supplied ms values multiplied by hz with no upper bound — i64 overflow wraps end_tick/prime_from
evidence:
if !ok_s || !ok_e || !ok_t || start_ms < 0 || end_ms <= start_ms || step_ms <= 0 {
...
	end_tick := u64(max(0, i64(end_ms) * i64(hz) / 1000))
...
	prime_from := u64(max(0, i64(start_ms) * i64(hz) / 1000))
detail: Validation only bounds the lower end; end_ms ≳ 4.6e17 makes i64(end_ms)*20 wrap, yielding a wrong end_tick (premature 'no frames rendered' exit or a window silently capped by demo ticks).
recommended_fix: Reject ms arguments above a sane ceiling (e.g. end_ms*hz must stay within i64) alongside the existing range check.

title: packet_interp_pos persists the from_screen (0,0) fallback as a world position when scale <= 0, smearing the next tick's glide base
detail: In a zero-size/minimized window during Run (alpha<1), the guard makes cur = world (0,0); the interp row stores it, so after restore the row rolls prev=(0,0) and the identity-continuous packet lerps from the map corner for one tick (no snap — anchors unchanged).
recommended_fix: Skip the cache write/lerp when v.scale <= 0 (render snapshot-exact, like alpha=1) so the degraded frame never seeds the glide base.
